headline: High-risk workflow automation pair: n8n can write and execute server-side actions, while awesome-prompts can feed untrusted prompt content into that workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository, so its outputs can be attacker-controlled text. n8n can ingest workflow inputs and route them into AI Agent nodes and other tools. The pair creates a plausible prompt-injection path if prompt content from agent_a is fed into agent_b without provenance checks; no direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF agent_a prompt text is copied into an n8n workflow input or AI Agent node
IF agent_b treats that text as instructions rather than data
IF no provenance or allowlist filter is applied before tool use
mitigations: Add a fixed system prompt that labels agent_a content as untrusted data
Insert a manual review step before any AI Agent node consumes prompt text
Strip tool directives and markdown from imported prompt content
Use a provenance tag or allowlist for approved prompt sources
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware in the workflow

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b has broad network egress, server filesystem access, and handles whatever the workflow processes, so sensitive workflow data can leave the system. agent_a is a prompt repository with no data classes touched, so it is not itself a sensitive-data source; the leakage risk is mainly that agent_b can expose workflow contents if agent_a-supplied prompts cause sensitive inputs to be processed or forwarded.
conditions: IF the workflow processes secrets, customer data, or internal documents
IF agent_b sends those contents to an external integration node or API
IF agent_a content is used to construct prompts that include sensitive context
mitigations: Restrict n8n credentials to least-privilege scopes
Disable or gate external integration nodes for sensitive workflows
Move secrets to a separate credential store and avoid prompt inclusion
Add a data-class check before any outbound node
requires-engineering: segment sensitive workflows onto a separate n8n instance

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b can write the server filesystem and execute shell/subprocesses, while agent_a is a content source that can influence workflow behavior. Even though agent_a cannot write, the pair still creates a dangerous overlap because n8n's shared server filesystem and execution nodes can be driven into conflicting writes or destructive actions by content-derived workflow logic; uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this to high.
conditions: IF two n8n executions target the same server path or shared datastore
IF workflow logic derived from agent_a content triggers file writes or shell commands
IF no external lock or per-job directory isolation is configured
mitigations: Write each run to a unique temp directory
Add a mutex or queue around file-writing steps
Disable Execute Command for workflows that ingest external prompt content
Use append-only outputs instead of in-place edits
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking and job isolation

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an orchestrator that can act on AI Agent outputs through downstream nodes, so if it treats agent_a's prompt content as authoritative, errors can cascade into real actions. agent_a provides prompt material rather than verified facts, and agent_b can execute shell or integration actions, making unverified content especially risky in default workflow designs.
conditions: IF agent_a output is used as an input to an AI Agent node or downstream automation step
IF agent_b performs actions without a human verification gate
IF the workflow maps generated text directly to emails, tickets, shell commands, or API calls
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before any action node
Require structured outputs with schema validation
Log and diff AI outputs before execution
Limit action nodes to read-only operations
requires-engineering: add policy checks that block unverified AI-to-action transitions

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b processes whatever the workflow handles and can send it to many integrations, so residency and retention obligations depend on the connected systems. agent_a is only a prompt repository and does not itself impose a residency regime, so the compliance risk is mainly from n8n's broad processing and logging surface rather than from agent_a.
conditions: IF the workflow processes regulated data such as EU PII or PHI
IF any connected integration stores or transmits that data outside the required jurisdiction
IF n8n logging or credential storage retains data longer than policy allows
mitigations: Review each integration's residency and retention settings
Avoid routing regulated data through generic AI workflows
Mask or redact sensitive fields before workflow execution
Set shorter log retention on the n8n server
requires-engineering: isolate regulated workflows into a compliant deployment
